categories.name: Keep
categories.hint: Authentic film look — visible (not faked-digital) grain, natural halation, period-correct colour science, sharp where intended, on-topic. OVR_Quality_Score >= 60 AND REL_Quality_Score >= 60

categories.name: Borderline
categories.hint: Reads as film but average — muddy scan, dust/scratches dominating, heavy colour cast, or only-okay quality. Bucket for human review

categories.name: DigitalLook
categories.hint: Clean clinical digital capture with no film characteristics (no grain, clipped highlights, sterile colour) -> off-theme for a film-emulation dataset

categories.name: OffTopic
categories.hint: Unrelated to the film-photography subject regardless of quality (REL_Quality_Score < 30)

preset.category_rules:
STRICT JUDGEMENT RULES (no exceptions):
- Fill `description` and `primary_subject` FIRST, from the pixels only. Then make every label agree with that description.
- art_medium = `photograph` ONLY for a camera-captured (or AI photoreal) image. A render, illustration or anime frame is NEVER `photograph`.
- has_ai_flaws = TRUE only for SEVERE artefacts (malformed face/hands, wrong finger count, melted limbs, warped text, impossible geometry).
- A COMPOSITE/GRID is 2+ separate images stitched together -> is_composite_grid=true and DISCARD.
- contains_text_overlay = TRUE for burned-in watermarks, captions, logos, or date stamps.
- nsfw = TRUE only for explicit nudity or sexual content.
This dataset trains a FILM-EMULATION LoRA. Reward genuine analog character (organic grain, gentle halation/bloom, period colour palettes, soft highlight roll-off). A sterile, grainless, clipped digital photo is DigitalLook (off-theme). The curation topic only informs REL_Quality_Score; do NOT invent details that aren't in the pixels.

scoring.notes: Reward organic film grain, smooth highlight roll-off, period-correct colour and a clear subject. Penalise faked/uniform digital noise, blown highlights, heavy dust/scratch damage and muddy low-res scans.
